generations.desc: Raw binary code (0s and 1s) directly executed by CPU hardware. Machine dependent, hardest to program.
Uses human-readable alphanumeric Mnemonics (e.g., ADD, MOV, SUB, JMP). Translated into machine code by an Assembler.
Machine-independent languages using English-like syntax and mathematical notations. Translated via Compilers or Interpreters.
generations.example: C, C++, Java, Fortran, COBOL, BASIC, Pascal

generations.desc: Non-procedural languages focusing on 'WHAT to do' rather than 'HOW to do it'. Closer to natural language.
Languages designed for artificial intelligence, expert systems, and problem-solving without programmer algorithm specifications.

sections.title: Language Translators: Compiler vs Interpreter vs Assembler
sections.hindiTitle: भाषा अनुवादक: कंपाइलर बनाम इंटरप्रेटर बनाम असेंबलर

translators.name: Compiler
translators.execution: Translates entire source code into machine/object code (.obj / .exe) in ONE single pass before execution.
translators.errorReporting: Displays all errors and warnings together after scanning entire file.

translators.name: Interpreter
translators.execution: Translates and executes source code LINE BY LINE. Does not generate intermediate standalone executable file.
translators.speed: Slower runtime execution compared to compiled code.
translators.errorReporting: Stops execution immediately at the very first syntax error encountered.

translators.name: Assembler
translators.execution: Translates low-level Assembly mnemonic programs into raw Machine Language object code.

translators.name: Hybrid (JIT / Bytecode)
translators.execution: Compiles source code into architecture-neutral intermediate Bytecode (.class file), which is interpreted/JIT compiled by a Virtual Machine (JVM / CLR).
translators.examples: Java (javac compiles to bytecode, JVM executes), C# (.NET CLR).

sections.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Pillars
sections.hindiTitle: ऑब्जेक्ट ओरिएंटेड प्रोग्रामिंग के चार स्तंभ

pillars.name: Class & Object
pillars.desc: A Class is a blueprint or user-defined prototype from which individual Objects (instances having state and behavior) are created.

pillars.name: Encapsulation
pillars.desc: Bundling data (attributes) and methods that operate on that data into a single unit (class), restricting direct access to internal components (Data Hiding using private access specifiers).

pillars.name: Abstraction
pillars.desc: Representing essential features while hiding internal background implementation details from user (e.g., ATM screen shows 'Withdraw Money' without revealing internal banking queries).

pillars.name: Inheritance
pillars.desc: Mechanism where a new class (derived/child class) inherits properties and behaviors from an existing class (base/parent class). Promotes code reusability.

pillars.name: Polymorphism
pillars.desc: 'Many forms'. Ability of a message, function, or operator to be processed in more than one way (Compile-time: Method Overloading; Runtime: Method Overriding).

structures.name: Array
structures.desc: Contiguous memory allocation storing elements of identical data type. Constant time $O(1)$ index access.

structures.name: Stack
structures.operations: Push (insert), Pop (delete), Peek (inspect top). Used in function call recursion, Undo operations, expression evaluation.

structures.name: Queue
structures.operations: Enqueue (insert at rear), Dequeue (remove from front). Used in printer spooling, CPU task scheduling.

structures.name: Linked List
structures.desc: Elements (nodes) connected via pointers/references, non-contiguous dynamic memory allocation (Singly, Doubly, Circular).

structures.name: Binary Tree
structures.desc: Hierarchical structure where each node has at most two children (Left and Right). Topmost node is Root; nodes with no children are Leaves.

structures.name: Graph
structures.desc: Collection of vertices (nodes) connected by edges (links). Models computer networks, social networks, GPS routes.

algorithms.name: Linear Search
algorithms.requirement: Works on unsorted or sorted array. Sequentially checks each item.

algorithms.name: Binary Search
algorithms.requirement: MANDATORY: Array MUST BE SORTED. Repeatedly divides search interval in half.

algorithms.name: Bubble Sort
algorithms.desc: Repeatedly swaps adjacent elements if in wrong order.
